title: console first load: metadata readers subscribe by selector instead of re-rendering on the store-wide version counter
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ② (the next lever a measured slice names) · Source: fleet (PR #37883, Part of #37575 and #37444: the thread's "What is left"; readings 7215089774 on #37444)

## What happens

After slices 1 and 2 of #37575, the list page's first load is 2685 ms and the record page's 2504 ms (h2 medians, 10 runs, same machine), both still over the 2500 ms target (#37444). The largest remaining cost the thread measured is the metadata store's single store-wide `version` counter: it is bumped six times before the list page's first paint, and every metadata reader re-renders on each bump, whatever it reads.

## Expected

- [ ] Metadata readers subscribe by selector (the item or slice they read) and re-render only when that answer changes; the store-wide counter stops driving renders.
- [ ] A render-count pin per reader family the profile names, red when a reader re-renders on an unrelated bump.
- [ ] Readings on #37444 as before (10 runs, h2 medians, list, record and home).

Grade: area:ux · enhancement · reach: every console page's first load · evidence: the thread's profile and readings
Suggested-grade: p2
Size: L
Related: #37575, #37444, PR #37883.
